plan.topic: Heartburn when you lie down at night on tirzepatide: what the label reports, and the NHS bedtime reflux habits
plan.angle: Sentence 1: 'Heartburn when you lie down on tirzepatide? Reflux is a listed, common side effect.' (14 words). Sentence 2 card: 'Reflux (GERD): 5% on tirzepatide 15 mg vs 2% on placebo, pooled weight trials in adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes.' An optional separate sentence can give indigestion at 10% vs 4%. Then the separate label sentence 'Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying.' with no 'so'. NHS habits, tagged NHS: 'Do not eat within 3 or 4 hours before bed.' and 'Raise the head of your bed by around 10 to 20 cm, so your chest and head are above your waist.' Untagged: ask a pharmacist before any antacid. Untagged: see your doctor if food gets stuck, you vomit often or you lose weight without trying. Chest pain, vomiting blood or black stools mean your local urgent care or emergency number. Close with the fixed don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. Post note target: Side Effects.
plan.why: A felt-symptom 'Is this normal?' moment for the morning slot. The bedtime angle is different from the 11-10 holiday-meal heartburn Short, and it feeds Side Effects, our top suggested-traffic earner. | fact-check: Checked. The Zepbound label's Table 2 (pooled Study 1 and Study 2, adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes) lists gastroesophageal reflux disease at 5% on 15 mg vs 2% on placebo, and dyspepsia at 10% on 15 mg vs 4% on placebo. The label sentence is "ZEPBOUND delays gastric emptying and thereby has the potential to impact the absorption of concomitantly administered oral medications." Use it only as the separate sentence 'Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying', with no causal link to heartburn. NHS wording checked: "do not eat within 3 or 4 hours before bed" and "raising the head of your bed by around 10 to 20cm, so your chest and head are above your waist, helps relieve symptoms." Fixes: (1) The label never says 'heartburn' or 'when you lie down', so sentence 1 must not suggest it does. Name the label terms. (2) Use one number per sentence and keep the pooled population on the card. (3) Add the NHS see-a-GP signs to the untagged urgent line: food getting stuck, frequent vomiting, unexplained weight loss. Keep chest pain, vomiting blood and black stools as emergency signs. (4) Cite the printed date of the exact label document you link. The HTML label shows 'Revised: 8/2026'.

package.title: Tirzepatide Heartburn at Night: 2 NHS Habits That Can Help #shorts
package.description:
On tirzepatide, reflux is a common label reaction (5% on 15 mg vs 2% on placebo, for up to 72 weeks). Two NHS bedtime habits can help.
For vomiting blood or black stools, call your local emergency number or get urgent care. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#Tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate and safe. I checked every claim against its source.
- **Hook and reflux numbers (S1):** The Zepbound label (HTML, prints "Revised: 8/2026") lists reflux (GERD) among the most common adverse reactions (≥5%). Table 1 gives 5% on 15 mg vs 2% on placebo. The pool is Study 1 + Study 2: 2,519 adults with obesity or overweight, treated "for up to 72 weeks".
- **Bedtime habits and doctor signs (S2):** The NHS heartburn page matches the wording almost exactly: "do not eat within 3 or 4 hours before bed"; raise the bed head "around 10 to 20cm, so your chest and head are above your waist"; a pharmacist can recommend antacids or alginates; see a GP for food getting stuck, being sick often or losing weight for no reason. Page last reviewed 20 November 2023.
- **Emergency line:** It's safe and matches NHS escalation. But S3 (Vomiting blood, reviewed 18 August 2025) lists black poo only alongside vomiting blood, not on its own, so the "black stools" half needs its own source. The NHS rectal-bleeding page covers it ("urgent GP appointment or… NHS 111 if your poo is black or dark red").
- **Word count:** 153 is correct (14/29/12/11/22/6/17/42).
- **Fixed safety lines and Shorts close:** The don't-stop line correctly uses "those emergency signs", and there's no subscribe or link line.

Fix the three minor items below before render.
